title: Three Tasty Vegan Sides on Repeat: Dairy-Free Mac and Cheese, Hazelnut Cauliflower Stuffing, and Broccoli Makeovers
summary: This Goodful video presents a trio of vegan, gluten-free side dishes with practical, drawable techniques. It opens with a dairy-free mac and cheese built on a potato-based base and a cashew cheese powder, using starchy pasta water to reach a creamy texture and finishing under a broiler with roasted tomatoes and gluten-free crackers. It then moves to a gluten-free stuffing centered on caramelized hazelnut cauliflower, flavored with a hazelnut paste enriched with parsley, garlic, lemon zest and juice, olive oil, and thyme, roasted until the hazelnuts caramelize. The third segment offers two broccoli preparations: a steamed broccoli variant topped with olive oil, salt, garlic powder, and quinoa, and a baby-broccoli variant roasted under a high-heat finish for crunch and lemon brightness. Throughout, the host emphasizes one-pot Dutch oven cooking to minimize cleanup, seasoning, and simple, vegetable-forward flavors suitable for gluten-free diets. The video concludes with a call to explore more gluten-free options and simple veggie ideas.

sections.description: The segment introduces a dairy-free, gluten-free mac and cheese that uses a boiled potato as a key base and a homemade cashew cheese powder. The powder (cashews, nutritional yeast, salt, onion, garlic) is blended with the potato and reserved starchy pasta water to achieve a creamy texture, with roasted tomatoes and gluten-free crackers added before a quick broil for finish.

sections.description: This section covers a gluten-free, stuffing-style dish: sautéed mushrooms, leeks, and shallots form the base, then a hazelnut paste (parsley, garlic, lemon zest, olive oil, thyme) is prepared and folded with cauliflower. The mixture is roasted at 350°F for about 45 minutes, with occasional mixing to encourage hazelnut caramelization and flavor balance. The chef notes adjusting lemon and salt if the result tastes bland.

sections.description: This section highlights a one-pot approach using a cast aluminum Dutch oven for a simple veggie-forward dinner. The cook seasons vegetables with oil, onion, garlic, ginger, paprika, and lemon zest/juice, then adds tomatoes and spinach to simmer down moisture. Quinoa is incorporated for protein, and a stock is used to flavor the dish. The host promotes the 'set it and forget it' mindset to minimize dishes and effort.
